newsitem.title: USA: CSX says sells some Conrail shares.
newsitem.headline: CSX says sells some Conrail shares.

text.p: CSX Corp. said Friday it sold 85,000 shares of Conrail Inc. on the open market Thursday to quash allegations that the size of its stake in the railroad company would trigger a Pennsylvania law that would require it to pay cash for all Conrail shares.
The contentions were made in court cases brought by Norfolk Southern Corp. and a Conrail shareholders group, which want CSX to pay cash for all their Conrail shares.

CSX agreed in December to pay $9.3 billion in stock and cash in a friendly merger with Conrail. Right after the merger partners revised terms of their deal, rebuffed bidder Norfolk Southern raised its all-cash offer by $500 million to $10.5 billion.
CSX said in documents filed with federal regulators that it sold the shares on the New York Stock Exchange at prices ranging from $98.875 to $99.125 per share.

Norfolk Southern and the Conrail shareholders group have argued in court documents that shares held by Conrail directors should be counted together with a 19.9 percent Conrail stake, or 17.9 million shares, acquired by CSX in a tender offer, thus giving CSX control of more than 20 percent and triggering the Pennsylvania law.

CSX, based in Richmond, Va., said it was selling the shares "to moot certain contentions" related to the law, but that it continued to believe the claims by Norfolk Southern and the shareholders group lacked merit.
CSX's stock rose 62.5 cents to $42.625, Conrail edged up 25 cents to $99.25 and Norfolk Southern gained $1 to $87 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
